The resulting sensor exhibits a broad detection range (7%–80% relative humidity (RH)), excellent linearity ( R 2 = 0.996), and high sensitivity (34.41 nF/% RH), attributed to its unique self-supplying ionic network built upon a highly conductive electronic backbone. The device’s simplicity and stability make it highly promising for wearable sensing applications, demonstrating a new strategy for designing smart sensors through synergistically coupling the electronic and ionic properties of materials.

title: Miniature bionic curved compound eye for high-precision imaging, recognition and tracking
abstract: Bionic compound eyes have emerged as a promising solution for high-precision and real-time imaging in complex scenarios, yet existing designs face challenges including poor imaging quality, low recognition efficiency, and difficulties in target tracking. To address these issues, this study proposes an ellipsoidal-ommatidia negative-meniscus-substrate compound eye (EONMSCE) tailored for planar optoelectronic detection. The EONMSCE features a honeycomb full-fill arrangement of ellipsoidal ommatidia, which optimizes imaging uniformity and enhances the brightness of edge ommatidia. High-precision fabrication of the EONMSCE was achieved via two-photon polymerization (TPP) lateral additive manufacturing. Optical performance validation using spot diagrams and modulation transfer function (MTF) analysis confirmed that the EONMSCE meets preset imaging requirements, with a measured field of view (FOV) of 82° that aligns well with the theoretical value of 82.2°. Compared to traditional spherical compound eyes, the EONMSCE increases edge ommatidia imaging brightness by up to 48%. To enable fast target acquisition and dynamic tracking, the YOLO11 visual algorithm was integrated into the EONMSCE system. Experimental results demonstrate that the trained YOLO11 model achieves a target recognition speed of 1.8 ms (corresponding to 555.56 Hz) and a recognition accuracy of 98.5% for Trypoxylus dichotomus , outperforming the 17 ms visual response speed of natural Drosophila . The model also exhibits stable and high-precision detection capabilities for small targets and targets under dim or high-intensity light conditions, with a minimum confidence score of 0.77. This work provides a practical technical reference for advancing the application of compound eye cameras in unmanned aerial vehicle obstacle avoidance, robotic visual navigation, industrial defect detection, and other related fields.

title: A multi-force microscale model for lunar dust detachment and dispersion induced by rover mobility
abstract: Lunar rover mobility inevitably induces dust lifting, posing risks to onboard instruments. This study develops a physics-based model that incorporates van der Waals forces, electrostatic interactions, and Coulomb forces to analyze the detachment and dispersion behavior of lunar dust. Numerical simulations using MATLAB are conducted to determine the critical detachment radius under varying driving speeds and slip rates. Results indicate that increasing either speed or slip rate reduces the detachment threshold from 19.11 to 17.79 µm. Further analysis of the simulated dust-dispersion images reveals a clear stratification in ejection height as a function of particle size. Under high-velocity and high-slip-rate conditions, small particles (radius < 20 µm) dominate the upper portion of the dust plume, reaching vertical propagation heights of up to 1.8 m, which substantially exceed the height of the rover itself. Validation against Apollo mission imagery confirms the model’s applicability. These findings provide theoretical guidance for dust mitigation strategies in future lunar rover missions.

title: A fine-grained, comprehensive, and quantitative rehabilitation assessment system based on depth camera
abstract: Stroke often results in upper and lower limb motor dysfunction, leading to prolonged rehabilitation training and assessment. Existing rehabilitation assessment methods rely on manual clinical scales, which have several limitations, such as strong subjectivity, partiality of the assessment, reliance on specialist physicians, and difficulty in capturing subtle changes. To address these challenges, we developed a fine-grained, comprehensive, quantitative automatic rehabilitation assessment system based on the depth camera for patients with upper and lower limb motor dysfunction. A joint motion capture platform is designed to collect visual temporal data of joint movements by using YOLOv8-Pose and the depth camera. We then proposed the trajectory-ROM-smooth (TRS) scoring algorithm based on joint motion data, which comprehensively and interpretably assesses patients’ rehabilitation level from the perspectives of joint tracking, flexion-extension, and muscle control ability. In the evaluation experiment of 21 stroke patients, the proposed system shows results highly consistent with the manual assessments of experienced physicians. More importantly, the TRS assessment results are more fine-grained and are able to sensitively capture subtle improvements of joints during the rehabilitation process. In conclusion, this work provides a fine-grained, comprehensive, and interpretable quantitative assessment for patients with motor dysfunction.

title: Enabling high-efficiency long-distance low frequency communication with a co-designed metamaterial transmitter and receiver
abstract: Very low frequency (VLF) communications have demonstrated significant application potential for cross-medium applications, including underground/underwater propagation, emergency communication, and navigation systems, owing to their superior penetration capability and low transmission loss in different media. However, the bulky size and short-range transmission remain huge obstacles to practical implementation. Addressing this issue may require high input power, radiation efficiency, and reception sensitivity. Therefore, a co-designed metamaterial transmitter and receiver scheme is proposed for miniature long-distance VLF communication. These metamaterial antennas, employing the synthetic optimization of isolation transformer, coupling resonance, and superposition amplification techniques, are co-designed for high-efficiency radiation and high reception sensitivity. Theoretical derivation, simulations, and experiments reveal the performance enhancement in input power, transmission efficiency, and transmission distance. Through these synergistic improvements in transmitting and receiving, the proposed VLF communication system enables reliable kilometer-level transmission and 48 m air-ground cross-medium transmission while maintaining a compact antenna size within λ /10000. Our work provides a universal optimization method for VLF antenna design, paving the way for applications in portable VLF devices, cross-medium communication, and indoor navigation.

title: Dimension-dependent electron-phonon interactions in silver nanomaterials for high-efficiency electrothermal conversion
abstract: Flexible electric heaters require materials with precise temperature control and rapid thermal response capabilities. In this work, we systematically investigate the influence of material dimensionality and nanoparticle deposition density on electrothermal conversion in silver nanomaterials. We found that variations in the contact modes among zero-dimensional (0D) silver nanoparticles significantly affect their electrothermal performance. Specifically, a lower deposition density results in relatively slender sintering necks, which enhance electron-phonon interactions and localized Joule heating effects, thus improving the electrothermal conversion efficiency. In contrast, a higher deposition density leads to more robust and thicker sintering necks, which reduces efficiency. Extending the study to one-dimensional (1D) silver nanowires, quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) silver flakes, and three-dimensional (3D) silver films, comparative analyses reveal a clear dimension-dependent hierarchy, with the order of electrothermal conversion efficiency being 0D > 1D > quasi-2D > 3D. As a demonstration, the fabricated Ag NPs/PI heater ( R s ∼3 Ω/sq, 2 cm × 2 cm) exhibits superior performance, with a rapid thermal response (∼250°C within 10 s), stable low-voltage operation (< 5 V), and high-temperature stability (∼250°C). This dimensional comparison reveals fundamental correlations between nanomaterial structure and electrothermal performance, establishing design principles for next-generation flexible heating systems.

title: Multi-mode coupled hair-like sensor for broadband hydrodynamic perception and direction identification
abstract: Aquatic organisms have evolved sophisticated hair-like sensory systems capable of detecting hydrodynamic flows with remarkable sensitivity and directionality. However, existing artificial hair-like flow sensors still face the challenges of directional discrimination and broadband sensitivity in underwater hydrodynamic perception. This study proposes a multi-mode coupled hair-like sensor (MMCHS) to overcome these limitations by mimicking the functional coordination found in seal whisker arrays. The MMCHS integrates four sensor units of distinct resonant frequencies into a centrally symmetric spiral-beam base. This architecture enables the fusion of their discrete resonant peaks into a collaborative broadband response, while the parameter-customized spiral beams introduce intrinsic structural anisotropy, thereby providing a physical mechanism for flow-direction identification. Through dynamic modeling and finite element analysis, the working principle enabling broadband perception and directional discrimination is characterized. Prototypes were fabricated and experimentally characterized under controlled hydrodynamic stimuli. Results demonstrate that the MMCHS exhibits a broad high-sensitivity frequency band, a linear response over flow velocities from 1 to 100 mm/s, and robust operation even under strong background noise (signal-to-noise ratio, SNR = −20 dB). When coupled with a basic classifier, the sensor achieves over 99% accuracy in simultaneously identifying both the type and direction of complex flow signals. The MMCHS thus provides a bio-inspired, integrated strategy for developing flow sensors capable of high-performance perception in complex aquatic environments.

title: High-temperature tribological properties of fabric/bismaleimide composites enhanced by hexagonal boron nitride
Carbon-Swallow Photovoltaic Modules—Perspective overview and preliminary study
abstract: Photovoltaics (PV) represent the most widely deployed solar energy technology and a cornerstone of sustainable power systems. However, conventional PV technologies still struggle with low solar-to-energy efficiency, thermally induced performance degradation, and carbon footprints throughout their life cycles. To address these challenges, this work presents the proposed Carbon-Swallow Photovoltaic Module, an integrated architecture comprising a PV layer, a thermo-carbon adjustment layer, and a microalgae carbon-fixation layer. This tri-layered design enables the simultaneous production of solar electricity, CO 2 sequestration, and sustainable high-value biomass. Notably, the thermo-carbon adjustment layer serves as a multi-functional interface that passively enhances energy and mass transfer within the system. By regulating vapor and CO 2 fluxes during diurnal and nocturnal cycles, the system achieves synergistic PV cooling and intensified microalgal photosynthesis. Outdoor experimental results on a 2 m 2 of test rig demonstrate that the system increased CO 2 replenishment by 18.5% and boosted microalgae biomass production by 22.6%, while maintaining a daily power output of 0.85 kWh. This strategy suggests a potential pathway for evolving solar farms from simple power plants into multifunctional solar-energy platforms that integrate clean electricity generation with CO 2 fixation and biomass production. However, quantitative carbon accounting and life-cycle assessment are still required to evaluate the net carbon balance of the proposed system.

title: Tunable mechanical properties in SLMed-TiBw/Ti6.5Al2.5Zr1Mo1V via precise regulation on microstructure
abstract: The incorporation of in-situ generated reinforcements into titanium alloys fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) has been demonstrated to significantly enhance mechanical strength while simultaneously reducing ductility. Post-heat treatment is commonly employed to optimize microstructural characteristics and improve mechanical performance. In this work, the influence of annealing temperature on the microstructure and mechanical properties of SLMed 0.85 vol.% TiBw/Ti6.5Al2.5Zr1Mo1V composites was systematically investigated. With increasing temperature, martensitic decomposition progressively intensifies, accompanied by microstructural coarsening and α-grain recrystallization, while the newly formed β phase maintains an orientation relationship with the parent martensite: \([{\bar 1}011]_{\alpha},//[1{\bar 1}{\bar 3}]_{\beta}, \, (10{\bar 1}{\bar 1})_{\alpha},//(201)_{\beta}\) . Variations in boron (B) atom diffusion coefficients, contents of β phase at different temperatures, and merging of TiBw led to a non-monotonic change in the aspect ratio of TiB whiskers, which initially increased and then decreased with rising temperature. Grain coarsening and reduced dislocation density were identified as the primary mechanisms underlying the reduction in strength, resulting in a progressive decrease in yield strength from 1231 MPa at 750°C to 939 MPa at 1000°C. In contrast, the increase in β-phase content, equiaxed grains, and enhanced interfacial bonding between the reinforcement and the matrix collectively contributed to improved ductility, with elongation increasing steadily from 7.8% at 750°C to 17.8% at 1000°C. These microstructural evolutions enable effective tailoring of the mechanical properties of SLMed-TiBw/Ti6.5Al2.5Zr1Mo1V composites, thereby offering targeted and instructive guidance for the fabrication of α/near-α titanium alloy matrix composites through SLM.

title: On irregular combustion of ammonia/hydrogen zero-carbon fuels under engine-relevant conditions
abstract: To mitigate greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel combustion, the transition to green energy is critical for the transportation sector. Ammonia (NH 3 ) has attracted significant attention as a zero-carbon fuel due to its high energy density and carbon-free combustion. However, its practical application is hindered by ignition difficulties and combustion instabilities. Hydrogen (H 2 ) blending has been proposed as an effective strategy to overcome these limitations. Yet, hydrogen enrichment also introduces irregular combustion phenomena, such as knocking and pre-ignition, which constrain engine performance. In this study, fundamental optical diagnostics combined with transient synchronous measurements were employed to investigate the mechanisms governing these irregular combustion behaviors. Results show that pure ammonia combustion under spark ignition is dominated by regular flame propagation, whereas hydrogen blending promotes irregular combustion. When the hydrogen blending ratio reaches ∼20%, end-gas auto-ignition becomes evident, while further increases beyond 40% lead to predominant knocking combustion. Pre-ignition occurs primarily at elevated temperatures, where the combustion mode transitions from flame-propagation-dominated to auto-ignition-dominated combustion. Moreover, a high hydrogen fraction significantly intensifies knocking due to enhanced chemical reactivity, whereas high temperature tends to induce weaker knocking due to reduced energy density. Finally, an auto-ignition mode diagram was constructed for ammonia/hydrogen mixtures, revealing a strong correlation between irregular combustion and combustion mode. Specifically, increasing the hydrogen fraction promotes detonation development, whereas pre-ignition occurring at high temperatures is characterized by subsonic deflagration, consistent with experimental observations. These findings provide new insights into the combustion characteristics of ammonia/hydrogen fuels and establish a theoretical basis for optimizing zero-carbon fuel engines.

title: LSTM neural network-based data-driven adaptive control for MIMO discrete-time systems
abstract: A long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network is integrated into a data-driven adaptive sliding mode control (SMC) strategy to enhance the tracking accuracy and robustness of the system. The designed controller only employs the input and output data without requiring the mathematical model or structural information of the system. Hence, the proposed method is data-driven. Firstly, based on the dynamic linearization method of the model-free adaptive control, a novel controller of multi-input multi-output (MIMO) nonlinear discrete-time systems is designed by combining with the SMC. Then, an LSTM network updated scheme is proposed via the backpropagation algorithm, which achieves real-time adjustment of the switching gain matrix, enabling more accurate execution of the control strategy. Subsequently, the convergence analysis of the adaptive SMC approach is provided through rigorous mathematical proofs, and the numerical simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method. Finally, we discuss the existing challenges.

title: Bio-inspired drag reduction surfaces: Synergistic integration of an imbricated tuna skin multilayered architecture with MOF-based superhydrophobic composite coatings
abstract: The hydrodynamic performance of underwater vehicles is significantly constrained by skin friction drag, which constitutes the predominant component of total resistance. Inspired by the imbricated array architecture of tuna skin scales and the exceptional surface characteristics of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), this study fabricates bio-inspired surfaces with gradient inclination angles via stereolithography 3D printing, followed by surface functionalization using an optimized spray-coating process. Systematic characterization confirms that the resulting modified biomimetic surface (MBS) 30° exhibits a water contact angle of 152.9°, indicating stable superhydrophobicity, and achieves an outstanding drag reduction rate of 92.1% in experimental tests, significantly surpassing the performance of individual structural or coating strategies. Durability and adhesion tests demonstrate remarkable mechanical robustness and excellent resistance to water erosion. Moreover, the surface displays efficient self-cleaning and anti-icing capabilities, while maintaining high drag reduction stability even under harsh chemical conditions including strong acids and alkalis. Numerical simulations reveal that the superior performance originates from the synergistic effect between the vortex-stabilizing biomimetic macrostructure and the interface slip induced by the ZIF-8 micro-nano structure. This study provides new insights and a technical pathway for developing high-performance drag-reduction coatings for marine equipment.

title: Experiment and analysis of non-uniform mismatch stresses in ultra-thin chips
abstract: Ultra-thin chips are designed to address the limitations of conventional chips in size scaling, power consumption, and thermal dissipation. Currently, they hold tremendous application potential in fields such as biomedical, artificial intelligence computing, and flexible electronics. However, chips thinner than 50 µm are typically manufactured using thinning or grinding processes, which inevitably introduce severe mismatch stresses and cause significant warpage, thereby limiting device performance and reliability. Moreover, the deformation driven by internal stresses such as misfit stresses or lattice mismatch in functional layers becomes significantly enhanced. This paper focuses on the ultra-thin chip structure, systematically investigating the evolution and suppression strategies of mismatch stresses through experimental measurements and theoretical analysis. White light interferometry was employed to measure warpage profiles and non-uniform curvatures of various ultra-thin chips. In terms of theoretical analysis, a multilayer thin film-substrate system mechanical model was established for mismatch stresses inversion. Furthermore, a patterned backside metallization design provides an effective method for mismatch stress control and chip planarization.

title: Self-organizing fuzzy tracking control for nonlinear systems with unknown multisource disturbances and its application
abstract: Unknown multisource disturbances always exist in nonlinear systems, especially in practical processes, which can enhance the adverse effect on the accuracy and stability of tracking control performance. To deal with this issue, a self-organizing fuzzy tracking control (SFTC) is developed to improve robustness. First, a self-organizing fuzzy neural network (SOFNN), based on the static and dynamic characteristics of neurons, is designed to approximate unknown terms of nonlinear systems. Then, the proposed model can comprehensively describe the system characteristics to assist in the tracking control. Second, a dynamic surface control (DSC) is integrated to avoid the differential explosion problem in traditional backstepping control, enabling high precision and fast trajectory tracking. Third, a Lyapunov function with tracking error, filtering error and estimation error (i.e., weight, center, and width of SOFNN parameters) is constructed to rigorously prove the stability of SFTC. It can be concluded from the theoretical proof that all closed-loop signals are semi-globally uniformly ultimately bounded (SG-UUB), and the tracking error converges to a small bounded region around zero. Finally, several simulation experiments and a real application of SFTC are conducted to validate its feasibility and effectiveness.

title: C2Mamba: Collaborative context state space model for remote sensing object detection
abstract: Object detection in remote sensing images (RSIs) is a fundamental and valuable task in the field of Earth observation and computer vision. Typically, RSIs are acquired from a bird’s-eye view, leading to inherent characteristics such as complex backgrounds, random and dense distribution of small objects, and large-scale variations. These characteristics significantly constrain the performance of existing object detectors. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight yet effective collaborative context state space model, C 2 Mamba, which integrates global context and multi-scale local receptive field information, thereby enabling higher accuracy for geospatial object detection. First, a collaborative multi-context Mamba is developed to capture diverse context information, including local, global, and channel-wise features, in a hierarchical interactive manner. This enables the generation of a comprehensive scene description that adaptively focuses on geospatial objects while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Second, a Gaussian large-receptive field perception module is designed to progressively aggregate context information and fine-grained details via increasingly larger receptive fields. This process is enhanced by a Gaussian modulation mechanism, which improves sensitivity to subtle yet discriminative features, thereby effectively addressing scale variations of remote sensing objects, especially for small ones. Experimental results on three public datasets (RSOD, NWPU VHR-10.v2, and DIOR) demonstrate that C 2 Mamba outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Deformation and breakage of carbonate sands: Coupled effects of particle size, initial shear stress, and loading stress path
abstract: Carbonate sand is prone to substantial deformation and particle breakage in marine and geotechnical engineering. Specifically, larger particles are generally more susceptible to crushing. Nevertheless, it remains unclear how these responses evolve as the loading stress path rotates from 0° to 90°. Furthermore, it becomes more complex when the specimens are prepared with different particle sizes or subjected to initial shear stress states. Addressing the above issues is experimentally challenging as the conditions mentioned above are complex, but studying the above issues is necessary as such conditions exist in the field. In this study, we investigated the coupled effects of particle size, loading stress path, and initial shear stress on the shear and breakage behaviors of carbonate sands (CS) through stress-controlled drained triaxial tests. For a given loading stress path, both deformation and particle breakage increase with particle size. Meanwhile, for a given particle size, the deformation mode transitions from a contraction-dominated mode to a shear-dominated mode as the loading stress path rotates counterclockwise from 0° to 90°. The particle breakage index remains nearly constant for loading path angles below 90° under isotropic conditions, and increases markedly at 90°. Under anisotropic consolidation, the particle breakage increases obviously from a loading path angle of 71.6° to 90°. Despite these distinct deformation and breakage patterns, a unique empirical equation was proposed to describe the relationship between particle breakage and soil deformation. These findings advance the understanding of breakage and deformation behaviors under different loading stress paths and provide practical guidance for the design of marine infrastructure on carbonate sand foundations.

title: Memristive complex-valued neural network: Chaotic dynamics, and its application to enhanced genetic algorithm
abstract: Chaotic systems can enhance stochastic optimization, but their performance is often limited by the dimensionality of the chaos source. This paper introduces a memristive complex-valued Hopfield neural network (MCVHNN) that generates high-dimensional complex-valued chaotic dynamics. The model’s complex behaviors, including multi-scroll attractors, are rigorously analyzed and physically validated on an field-programmable gate array (FPGA). Furthermore, the MCVHNN is employed as a chaos generator for a complex-valued genetic algorithm (CVGA) in robotic path planning. The CVGA utilizes complex encoding and chaotic geometric operators, demonstrating superior performance in success rate and path quality over conventional methods. This work establishes an integrated framework linking a novel chaotic system to enhanced intelligent optimization.

title: A mechanical metamaterial with tunable Poisson’s ratio and modulus for non-uniform deformation
abstract: Mechanical metamaterials with tunable properties have attracted considerable attention in recent years. This paper presents a novel lattice metamaterial composed of inclined beams, whose macroscopic behavior is governed by three independent angular parameters ( α, β , and θ ). A theoretical framework based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory is established to predict the elastic modulus and Poisson’s ratio, and is validated through finite element simulations and quasi-static tensile experiments on 3D-printed thermoplastic polyurethane specimens. The results demonstrate three key capabilities. First, the Poisson’s ratio can be continuously tuned over an exceptionally wide range from −1.07 to 0.74, surpassing most existing designs. Second, quantitative sensitivity analysis reveals that β governs lateral deformation with negligible influence on stiffness, while α and θ play a coordinated regulatory role. This confirms significant decoupling of Poisson’s ratio and modulus. Third, by integrating unit cells with distinct Poisson’s ratios into a cylindrical configuration, we achieve spatially programmable radial expansion under axial loading, with the middle segment expanding radially and the top/bottom segments contracting. This capability offers a promising strategy for next-generation biomedical stents requiring lesion-specific dilation. This study provides a versatile design framework for lightweight, multifunctional materials requiring precise deformation control.

title: Whole-process control of dioxins in electric arc furnace flue gas: Progress, challenges, and prospects
abstract: Against the backdrop of the accelerating green and low-carbon transformation of the steel industry, electric arc furnace (EAF) short-process steelmaking has expanded rapidly owing to its remarkable advantages in energy conservation and carbon emission reduction. However, dioxin emissions from EAF flue gas have emerged as a critical obstacle to achieving clean production in the steel industry. The major barriers to the long-term stable compliance of dioxin emissions from EAF flue gas mainly include insufficient control of chlorine-containing and organic impurities in scrap at the source, inadequate suppression of dioxin resynthesis during the flue gas cooling stage, and the limited adaptability of single end-of-pipe treatment technologies under complex and fluctuating operating conditions. Compared with relying solely on end-of-pipe treatment, establishing a whole-process collaborative control system encompassing source-stage scrap sorting and pretreatment, process optimization to improve combustion and suppress dioxin formation, and efficient end-of-pipe treatment is an important pathway for achieving ultralow dioxin emissions from EAF flue gas. Future research should prioritize the development of intelligent and precise regulation of flue gas operating conditions, synergistic multipollutant control technologies, high-efficiency and low-cost treatment materials, and highly comprehensive systems for emission standards, online monitoring, and engineering performance evaluation. The establishment of a whole-process collaborative control system will provide a solid theoretical basis and technical support for the long-term reduction of dioxin emissions, thereby facilitating the green and high-quality development of the EAF steelmaking industry.

title: Lightweight convolutional neural network based on overlapping kernel compression pruning for modeling nonlinear systems
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) stack numerous convolutional kernels to model nonlinear systems by filtering spatial features. However, overlapping kernels with similar spatial weight arrangements introduce spurious correlations from repeated feature extraction, which results in high computational cost and limited generalization capability. To address this issue, a lightweight CNN (LCNN) based on overlapping kernel compression pruning is proposed in this paper. First, an overlapping kernel perception (OKP) method is designed to assess the kernel redundancy of LCNN. The OKP method adopts spectral clustering to group similar kernels into the graph Laplacian spectral space. It broadens the redundancy scope by incorporating overlapping kernels with similar spatial weight arrangements. Second, a kernel compression pruning (KCP) strategy is built to prune redundant kernels. Guided by kernel redundancy, the KCP strategy performs singular value decomposition on each group of similar kernels and adaptively truncates the rank of the decomposed matrix to reconstruct a compact set of representative kernels. Third, a regularized gradient descent algorithm is developed to fine-tune the parameters of LCNN after pruning. Finally, experimental results on three industrial datasets confirm the superior generalization performance of LCNN compared to other models.

title: Ultrahigh anisotropic mobility and strong polarization-sensitive photocurrent response in ZnO/SeMoSiP2 van der Waals heterojunction: A first-principles study for advanced photodetectors
abstract: In this study, we systematically explored the structural stability, electronic-optical properties, and photodetection potential of ZnO/SeMoSiP 2 van der Waals heterojunctions via first-principles calculations. SeMoSiP 2 (direct bandgap: 1.37 eV) has a 3.7% lattice mismatch with ZnO; the ZnO/Se (Se-side stacked) and ZnO/P (P-side stacked) heterojunctions are ther-modynamically, kinetically, and mechanically stable. Both are type-I direct bandgap semiconductors (1.34 eV), exhibiting interfacial charge transfer and a built-in potential difference. ZnO/Se exhibits higher carrier mobility (max electron: 405 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ; max hole: 1450 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ) and weak anisotropy, while ZnO/P shows remarkable electron mobility anisotropy ( Y/X = 4.61). The heterojunctions have significantly enhanced visible-light absorption (max 2.9 × 10 5 cm −1 ) vs. pristine materials, with bandgaps and absorption peaks tunable by biaxial strain. Photodetection simulations show ZnO/Se (armchair direction) achieves a 16.1 a 2 0 /photon peak photocurrent at 517 nm (outperforming traditional semiconductors), and ZnO/P (zigzag direction) has a maximum polarization extinction ratio of 45. This work proposes a high-performance ZnO/SeMoSiP 2 system, clarifies the interface-driven anisotropic photoresponse mechanism, and supports designing high-sensitivity, polarization-selective photodetectors.

title: Semantics-guided contrastive pre-training with cluster-aware decision making for zero-shot bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Although existing cross-domain diagnosis models have mitigated the challenge of data scarcity, their performance degrades significantly in complex production scenarios where sparse fault impulses are heavily masked by non-stationary noise. To overcome this limitation, this study proposes fault diagnosis contrastive language-signal pre-training (FD-CLSP), a zero-shot cross-domain framework for bearing fault diagnosis under unseen operating conditions that leverages the noise-robustness and domain-invariance of high-level semantics to guide the extraction of elusive physical features. First, the adaptive vibration signal (AVS) encoder incorporates a hybrid prompt mechanism. Leveraging linguistic priors to act as a semantic filter, it steers the model’s attention to impulse-rich temporal segments while suppressing background interference. Second, to address the sparsity where local fault patterns are submerged in noise, a cluster decision-making (CDM) module is proposed. Through unsupervised clustering, this module decouples discriminative fault patterns from noise-dominated segments, enabling robust, evidence-based decisions without target domain labels. FD-CLSP achieves an average zero-shot accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline by over 7 percentage points, and attains a highly reliable expected calibration error (ECE) of 1.35%.

title: A bioinspired pneumatic finger pad sensor for simultaneous recognition of coupled tactile features
abstract: Mimicking the human sense of touch is essential for endowing robots with the capability to interact intelligently with their surroundings. However, effectively recognizing the inherently coupled features of objects (e.g., stiffness and shape) remains a significant challenge, as traditional sensors often struggle with signal ambiguity under complex contact conditions. Inspired by the multilayered structures of the human finger pad, this study developed a novel bioinspired pneumatic finger pad sensor (PFPS). The PFPS features a vertically integrated design with a pneumatic cavity that provides mechanical compliance for surface adaptation. Crucially, it achieves stimulus detection via a top resistive layer and a bottom capacitive layer that simultaneously achieve local strain sensing and global pressure monitoring, respectively. By fusing these complementary modalities, the PFPS effectively decouples mixed mechanical stimuli. A robust tactile sensing system was established by integrating the PFPS with machine learning algorithms, thereby achieving high-precision recognition for different coupled features, including moving direction and shape (100%), stiffness and shape (95.5%), and contact conditions (94.4%). This work offers a structurally integrated solution for resolving signal ambiguity in tactile perception, significantly enhancing the capability of robots to understand and manipulate their surroundings.

title: Al2O3@N-doped carbon/MXene arrays for superior fluoride removal in capacitive deionization
abstract: The performance of traditional Al 2 O 3 in defluorination is constrained by its inherent poor conductivity and particle agglomeration, calling for novel material designs to overcome these bottlenecks. In this work, a hierarchical array-structured Al 2 O 3 @NC/MXene was synthesized via an in situ growth-confined carbonization strategy under solvent-free and room-temperature conditions. This architecture integrates multiple electron transport pathways, abundant ion diffusion channels, and highly dispersed specific adsorption sites. The effects of MXene content and carbonization temperature were systematically investigated. When applied as an anode material in capacitive deionization (CDI) for fluoride removal, the Al 2 O 3 @NC/MXene- M -800 ( M = 59.9 mg MXene; 800°C) electrode exhibited an ultrahigh fluoride uptake capacity of 80.05 mg g −1 , a high instantaneous adsorption rate of 6.27 mg g −1 min −1 (100 mg L −1 F − solution at 1.4 V), and excellent cycling stability with 90.2% capacity retention after 40 cycles. The in situ assembly and confined carbonization strategy effectively mitigates the inherent limitations of conventional Al 2 O 3 , namely its poor electrical conductivity and tendency to agglomerate. This approach not only broadens its application in high-performance electrochemical separation but also paves the way for designing advanced CDI electrode materials through the constructed hierarchical array architecture.

title: Multi-variant γ lamellar evolution in γ-TiAl alloys
abstract: Abstract The morphology of nanoscale γ lamellae strongly influences the mechanical properties of fully lamellar Ti-Al alloys; however, the coarsening mechanisms governing these nanostructures remain poorly understood. This work combines phase-field simulations and experiments to investigate the growth and coarsening of γ lamellae. It reveals multiple lamellar orientation-dependent coarsening mechanisms, including coalescence, Ostwald ripening, and internal interface migration. The simulated planar or step-like γ/γ interfaces agree well with the experimental observations. The competing effects between elastic energy and chemical driving force on the evolution kinetics of γ lamellae are quantitatively characterized. Elevated elastic energy suppresses coarsening and refines the lamellar structure, whereas a large chemical driving force accelerates precipitation, coarsening, and splitting. A four-stage kinetic sequence is identified for γ lamellar evolution: nucleation and growth, quasi-steady-state coarsening, splitting, and steady-state coarsening. These findings offer novel insights into the complex coarsening mechanisms and kinetic pathways of multi-variant γ lamellae in γ-TiAl alloys.

title: Bispecific cell engagers: Evolving construction strategies, clinical progress, and future perspectives
abstract: Bispecific cell engagers (BsCEs) have emerged as a promising class of cancer immunotherapeutics, exerting robust antitumor activity by bridging immune effector and tumor cells to trigger potent, MHC-independent tumor lysis. Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) represent the predominant class of BsCEs currently in use, with 13 approved therapies validating their notable clinical efficacy across multiple tumor indications. However, the inherent complexity of protein engineering limits their broader clinical translation and widespread application. Persistent challenges, including heavy and light-chain mispairing, suboptimal structural stability, and enhanced costs associated with large-scale production, have driven researchers to explore alternative, more feasible construction paradigms. This paper systematically reviews the evolutionary landscape of BsCEs manufacturing technologies. First, mainstream genetic engineering strategies, encompassing the fragment assembly approach and IgG-like platforms, which currently serve as a gold standard for BsCEs development, are summarized. Subsequently, emerging interdisciplinary approaches that overcome traditional biosynthetic bottlenecks are highlighted. These include site-specific chemical conjugation for controllable modular assembly, antibody–nanoparticle conjugates that leverage the enhanced permeability and retention effect to optimize solid tumor targeting, and synthetic alternatives such as bispecific aptamers and peptides. A comprehensive analysis of these diverse approaches elucidates technical advantages by addressing key barriers to clinical translation. A forward-looking roadmap for the research and development of next-generation bispecific immunotherapeutics is outlined.

title: Recent advances and challenges of ZnIn2S4-based photocatalysts in the energy and environment fields
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic technology is regarded as a highly promising technology for energy conversion and environmental remediation due to its green, clean, and low-cost features. The development of photocatalysts with high activity and excellent cycling stability is the key to promoting the practical application of photocatalytic technology. Among numerous photocatalytic materials, ZnIn 2 S 4 has received considerable attention owing to its suitable band structure and outstanding photochemical properties. It has been widely applied in various fields including water splitting for H 2 production, CO 2 reduction, green synthesis of H 2 O 2 , and degradation of organic pollutants. This work systematically summarizes the latest research progress of ZnIn 2 S 4 -based photocatalysts in the fields of energy conversion and environmental remediation, and comprehensively elaborates on the modification strategies including defect engineering, heterostructure construction, microstructural design, and cocatalyst modification. Furthermore, based on the analysis of the reaction mechanism for ZnIn 2 S 4 -based photocatalysts, we deeply reveal the intrinsic relationship between the inherent characteristics and catalytic performance. Finally, we summarize the existing challenges in this field and prospect the future development directions, aiming to provide important references for the design of high-efficiency photocatalysts and the sustainable development of society.

title: Polypyrrole-mediated photothermal catalysis for nitroarenes reduction over urchin-like dual-active-sites catalyst
abstract: Metal sulfide-based photothermal materials have attracted significant attention for catalytic applications; however, their development faces intrinsic limitations such as rapid recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, limited photostability, and a scarcity of accessible active sites. To address these challenges, we developed a rationally designed photothermal catalyst consisting of uniformly dispersed Pd species anchored on polypyrrole (PPy) functionalized urchin-like bismuth sulfide (Bi 2 S 3 ) microspheres. Crucially, the conductive and photothermal PPy layer not only mediates efficient interfacial charge transfer, significantly suppressing carrier recombination and enhancing photogenerated electron utilization, but also acts as a protective barrier, mitigating sulfur poisoning of the Pd species by isolating them from direct contact with the Bi 2 S 3 substrate. The resultant Pd/Bi 2 S 3 @PPy photothermal catalyst possesses dual active sites (i.e., Pd and Bi 2 S 3 ) and exhibits a high photothermal conversion efficiency under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation. In the reduction reaction of nitroarenes with NaBH 4 , the Pd/Bi 2 S 3 @PPy demonstrates high photothermal catalytic activity, favorable stability, and broad substrate applicability. This work establishes a rational design strategy for developing highly efficient and stable photothermal catalysts, offering broad potential for advancing NIR-driven chemical transformations.

title: Hybrid hydrogel electrodes for highly stretchable and high-capacitance flexible supercapacitors
abstract: Flexible supercapacitors (FSCs), driven by the urgent demand for lightweight and multifunctional wearable electronics, have rapidly advanced owing to their simple configuration, high electrochemical stability, and power density. However, achieving high specific capacitance and stable output under extreme deformations, particularly large tensile strains, remains a critical challenge. Herein, we report an intrinsically stretchable PVA/PEDOT/CNT/PANI hybrid hydrogel (PVCPH), engineered through sequential freeze-salting-out and acid treatment to form a 3D hierarchical framework. In this architecture, the PVA backbone provides reversible macroscopic elasticity, the PEDOT/CNT network establishes a continuous mesoscopic pathway for charge transport, and proton-doped PANI nanospheres serve as highly effective microscopic pseudocapacitive contributors. Owing to this hierarchical integration, PVCPH exhibits remarkable stretchability (301.35%±5.46%) while delivering a high specific area capacitance (CA) of 2001 mF cm −2 . Even in quasi-solid-state devices with gel electrolytes, the FSCs maintain a CA of 1513 mF cm −2 and achieve an outstanding energy density of 135 µWh cm −2 . Furthermore, the devices preserve nearly 100% capacitance after repeated cycles of stretching, bending, and twisting, highlighting their robustness under extreme mechanical conditions. These results establish a viable strategy for designing deformation-tolerant FSCs capable of powering next-generation wearable electronics.

title: Boosted in-situ self-Fenton photocatalytic purification of metronidazole on g-C3N4/CdIn2S4
abstract: Designing photocatalytic materials with efficient hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) generation and pollutant purification capabilities remains a significant challenge. Herein, a novel carbon-doped g-C 3 N 4 /CdIn 2 S 4 heterojunction (denoted C-GCN/CIS) was designed to synergistically couple visible-light-driven in-situ H 2 O 2 generation with a Fe 2+ -activated self-Fenton process for efficient metronidazole (MTZ) removal. The optimized C-GCN/CIS-50 catalyst exhibited a high H 2 O 2 production rate of 5762 µmol g −1 h −1 , which, upon Fe 2+ activation, generated hydroxyl radicals (·OH), achieving a 79.2% total organic carbon (TOC) reduction within 60 min. Mechanistic studies revealed that interfacial charge redistribution enhances electron transfer from CdIn 2 S 4 (CIS) to carbon-doped g-C 3 N 4 (C-GCN), promoting charge separation and optimizing the adsorption/desorption of key oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates. Active-site analysis identified the interfacial nitrogen atom as the primary adsorption center for end-on *OOH. Upon *OOH binding, the Bader charge on this nitrogen atom changed significantly, highlighting its key role in interfacial charge reorganization and *OOH formation. These findings establish the interfacial N atom as the central active site for selective H 2 O 2 generation. Overall, this work introduces a novel heterojunction photocatalyst for efficient in-situ self-Fenton remediation and offers mechanistic insights into interfacial engineering and active-site regulation for advancing photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production and Fe-ion cycling.

title: Predictive tool condition monitoring framework for multi-pass boring operations in airplane intersection hole manufacturing
abstract: Machining quality of intersection holes is critical in the final assembly of airplanes, as it directly affects the structural integrity and fatigue life of the airplane. The boring process for intersection holes, a precision machining operation, typically involves multi-pass boring strategies, i.e., initial roughing passes followed by finishing passes, to effectively control cutting forces, thermal deformation, and machining-induced stresses. Tool condition monitoring (TCM) is particularly critical during this boring process, allowing real-time monitoring of tool wear or damage, thereby preventing the amplification of machining errors and potential workpiece scrapping. In multi-pass boring operations, tool wear progressively develops, meaning the tool’s current condition inherently depends on its state in prior passes. Consequently, conventional methods that rely only on the current boring pass to predict tool conditions are insufficient for this study. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces an innovative online predictive TCM framework utilizing a matrix long-short-term memory network. The proposed approach effectively captures the interdependencies across consecutive boring passes. By integrating historical boring signals with the current operational data, the proposed framework accurately predicts the real-time tool wear value of the current boring, delivering precise and timely tool condition insights for production line engineers. To validate the proposed framework, we built an experimental platform for the boring process of airplane intersection holes on a three-axis CNC machine that is equipped with an angular head. Experimental results validate the proposed framework, demonstrating superior predictive accuracy and robustness compared to conventional methods; the prediction error of the flank wear is less than 5 µm in MAE and RMSE metrics, providing a reliable solution for online TCM task.

title: A geometric approach for dynamic modeling of constrained multibody systems based on projective geometric algebra
abstract: Dynamic modeling of constrained multibody systems is essential for the simulation and control of parallel robotic systems. Building upon existing geometric frameworks for robot motion representation, such as dual quaternions, screw theory, and Lie groups, geometric algebra offers a unified formulation that enables more compact symbolic manipulation of geometric entities. In this paper, a geometric modeling approach for constrained multibody systems is developed within the framework of projective geometric algebra (PGA). The formulation uses explicit PGA representations of points, lines, and planes, together with meet and join operations. Based on these elements, the kinematics, the composite rigid body algorithm, and the constrained dynamic equations are derived in a unified PGA framework. The proposed method considers multibody systems subject to holonomic constraints, including fixed environmental constraints and cut-joint constraints. A consistent differentiation procedure in PGA is used to convert displacement-level geometric constraints into acceleration-level constraint equations. Simulation results on constrained robotic systems show that the proposed approach achieves numerical accuracy comparable to reference methods, while retaining a direct geometric representation of the constraints and competitive computational performance in the tested cases.

title: Poly(arylene-pyridine) membranes with adjusted aromatic structures for high temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: High-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT-PEMFCs) are promising candidates for efficient and clean energy conversion; however, their performance is still constrained by the trade-off between proton conductivity and mechanical stability in phosphoric acid (PA)-doped polymer electrolyte membranes. In this work, a series of poly(arylene-pyridine) copolymers were synthesized via superacid-catalyzed polyhydroxyalkylation by incorporating various fused-ring or bulky aromatic comonomers, including dibenzofuran (DBF), fluorene (Flu), 9,9-dimethylfluorene (DMF), and 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPHA), into the poly(terphenyl acetylpyridine) (PTAP) backbone. The influence of these aromatic architectures on thermal and chemical stability, PA doping and retention, hydrogen-bonding interactions, dimensional swelling, proton conduction, and mechanical strength was systematically investigated. Among them, the DBF-containing copolymer P(TP 80% -co-DBF 20% ) exhibited a well-balanced combination of high PA uptake (189%), low swelling, and excellent tensile strength (11.0 MPa). The DBF units not only disrupted compact polymer-chain stacking to generate additional free volume but also introduced oxygen bridges that served as multiple hydrogen-bonding sites, thereby constructing continuous proton-conducting networks. Consequently, the P(TP 80% -co-DBF 20% )/189%PA membrane achieved a high proton conductivity of 89.2 mS cm −1 at 180°C and delivered a peak power density of 816 mW cm −2 at 200°C under non-humidified H 2 /O 2 conditions. Comparative analysis revealed that variations in aromatic structure directly modulate polymer chain rigidity, acid-polymer affinity, and mechanical stability, thereby determining the conductivity-mechanical property balance. These findings highlight dibenzofuran as an ideal structural segment for PTAP-based HT-PEMs and establish a versatile molecular design strategy for next-generation high-performance polymer electrolyte membranes in HT-PEMFCs.

title: Polyethylene terephthalate microplastic aging mediated by Shewanella oneidensis via extracellular electron transfer under anoxic conditions
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate microplastics (PET-MPs) accumulate widely in natural environments, where microorganisms can substantially affect their aging. While previous studies on the microbial aging of PET-MPs have predominantly focused on oxidative and hydrolytic pathways, this study investigated the potential reductive aging of PET-MPs under anaerobic conditions using the model extracellular respiratory bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1. Our results showed that S. oneidensis MR-1 mediated the reductive aging of PET-MPs, as evidenced by substantial surface erosion, an 11.7% decrease in Young’s modulus, a 23.8% reduction in the O/C atomic ratio, and a 14.9%–26.5% loss of key oxygen-containing functional groups (C=O and C–O bonds). This aging process required extracellular electron transfer capability via the CymA-MtrABC-OmcA protein complex and flavin shuttles, as it was abolished by knockout of cymA and mtrABC-omcA and accelerated by the addition of exogenous flavin. Based on density functional theory calculations, including analysis of constrained Fukui functions and thermodynamic assessments, together with the detection of intermediates, a putative reductive aging pathway was proposed, in which the carbonyl group in the ester bond of PET-MPs was identified as the primary site susceptible to reduction. In the presence of PET-MPs, biomass retention and cell viability were both substantially higher than in the MP-free control, indicating that the reduction of PET-MPs sustained cellular survival under electron acceptor-limited conditions. These findings broadened the mechanistic understanding of the anaerobic PET aging process, which was underappreciated yet potentially important in oxygen-depleted environments.

title: High time resolution analysis of atmospheric particulate sulfur-nitrogen-containing organic compounds in Shanghai using a versatile aerosol concentration enrichment system
abstract: Sulfur-nitrogen-containing organic compounds (CHNS and CHONS) are potentially important constituents of organic aerosols (OAs). However, high-time-resolution molecular characterization of these compounds remains limited, leaving their rapid diurnal variations and sensitivity to short-term emission fluctuation poorly constrained. Here, we used a versatile aerosol enrichment system (VACES) to conduct a 3-hour resolution online sampling of urban aerosols in Shanghai, coupled with HPLC-Q-TOF-MS in both positive and negative ion modes for molecular identification and quantification. Many more molecules were detected in the negative ion mode, with 3567 CHONS and 460 CHNS formulas detected. Three-hourly profiles showed distinct diurnal patterns for partially oxidized versus highly oxidized CHONS, indicating different sources and formation pathways. In addition, six most intense nitrooxy-organosulfates were identified in this study, with two quantitatively analyzed for their diurnal variations. Both compounds exhibited significantly higher concentrations at night, suggesting nocturnal oxidation as a key source for these CHONS. Furthermore, motivated by their high intensities and potential toxicity, six benzothiazoles associated with tire-wear particles were also identified and quantified. Among them, benzothiazole-2-sulfonic acid and 2-hydroxybenzothiazole exhibited mean concentrations of 26.2 and 6.8 ng m −3 , respectively, far exceeding previously reported levels. Subsequent analysis suggested that elevated temperatures and secondary reactions may promote the concentration of 2-hydroxybenzothiazole. Overall, this work demonstrates the utility of high-resolution online sampling for resolving the molecular diversity of sulfur-nitrogen-containing organic compounds. It also provides new insights into their sources and evolution in urban aerosols.

title: Pinning control for delayed multiplex networks: Generalized criteria based on novel Halanay-type inequality
abstract: Multiplex networks is a frontier in complex network research, effectively characterizing the dynamics of interconnected real-world systems. Achieving pinning synchronization in such networks remains challenging under complex conditions involving both time-varying coupling delays and weights. This challenge is particularly salient when the delay function is non-differentiable, a scenario where existing theoretical frameworks still exhibit limitations. To address these issues, this study proposes two novel sets of Halanay-type inequalities with time-varying delays. Based on the Halanay inequality approach, sufficient pinning synchronization criteria are established for multiplex networks with time-varying coupling delays. The criteria elucidate the intricate interplay between control strategies and the admissible threshold of the delay. The theoretical framework reveals that the average values and fluctuations of time-varying control gain and coupling weight functions play a crucial role in network synchronization. Finally, numerical examples are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical results.

title: Event-triggered distributed control with state-dependent dynamic threshold for SoC balancing in islanded DC microgrids
Stability-oriented optimal configuration method based on DMSCR for long/short-duration energy storage systems
abstract: Although the traditional optimal configuration method for long/short-duration energy storage systems (ESSs) has been widely researched, it focuses more on system economy and cost. Furthermore, it neglects to assess the impact of energy storage (ES) support capacity on system voltage stability under different configurations, and does not consider how to maximize ES support capacity. Therefore, this paper proposes a stability-oriented optimal configuration method based on DMSCR. First, a hybrid power system model is constructed, and the dynamic multi-infeed short-circuit ratio (DMSCR) indicator is proposed to effectively and quantitatively characterize the ability of ES to support grid strength. Second, a three-tier ES optimal configuration framework is designed with the goal of improving support capacity and cost constraints in mind. It achieves the lowest economic cost and optimal configuration of ES grid connection nodes and capacity. Third, a Newton-Raphson-based iterative optimization approach is developed to address the configuration problem. On this basis, the optimal configuration of ESSs is formulated as an optimization problem with eigenvalue constraints. It can effectively suppress local optima traps while improving convergence efficiency and reducing the number of iterations. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed stability-oriented optimal configuration method based on DMSCR is effective.

title: Evaluation of heat exchange performance of energy piles with spiral pipes at the district scale
abstract: Shallow geothermal energy offers a promising renewable solution for urban energy transition. Large-scale utilization of energy piles for district heating and cooling can significantly contribute to building decarbonization. This study proposes a novel framework to evaluate the heat exchange performance of energy piles with spiral pipes and the spatiotemporal evolution of the soil temperature field at the district scale. By integrating a finite-length ring-coil heat source model with a GIS-based spatial proximity search algorithm, the method accurately accounts for the complex thermal interference between piles. A case study at Hohai University, China, demonstrated that the total annual cooling and heating potential provided by energy piles was 18972.7 MWh and 29029.6 MWh, respectively. After 120 d of cooling, the soil temperature at 7 m depth increased by 22.4°C, while it decreased by 24.4°C after 90 d of heating. Optimization analysis revealed that increasing the coil pitch from 0.2 to 0.5 m reduced the total cooling potential by 9.2%, whereas reducing the daily operation time ratio from 1.0 to 0.6 enhanced it by 59.6%. Crucially, compared to existing methods, the proposed approach more accurately distinguishes the varying degrees of thermal interference experienced by piles at building edges versus central zones, improving the prediction accuracy of the total heat exchange potential by 7.4%. These findings provide valuable references for the precise design and large-scale deployment of energy piles in urban districts.

title: AI-enhanced and data-driven mechanical analysis and structural topology optimization
abstract: Recent advances have underscored the transformative potential of integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and data science with computational mechanics, offering powerful new tools to tackle long-standing challenges in mechanical analysis and topology optimization. Notable progress includes predictive modeling of material behavior under complex loading conditions, real-time structural optimization, elucidation of microstructure-property relationships, acceleration of multiscale simulations, and data-driven discovery of novel materials and structural designs, among others. These AI-enhanced techniques enable unprecedented accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, ushering in a data-centric paradigm for addressing intricate engineering problems. Despite these promising developments, challenges include data quality and accessibility, the black-box nature and interpretability issues, high computational demands in data collection, and integrating AI models with established engineering workflows. Overcoming these barriers calls for coordinated interdisciplinary efforts to promote data standardization and sharing, enhance model transparency and robustness, and combine the advantages of both the AI methodologies and classical mechanics. This review systematically surveys recent progress at the intersection of AI and computational mechanics, highlights key challenges, and discusses emerging trends and future directions. By offering a concise overview, it aims to inspire further interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation, driving the development of AI-enhanced and data-driven methods for mechanical analysis, topology optimization, and beyond.

title: Bayesian sparse tensor wheel decomposition for missing data recovery
abstract: Tensor wheel (TW) decomposition is a powerful technique for analyzing high-dimensional data, offering a favorable balance between computational efficiency and expressive power. However, its performance is critically sensitive to rank specification, with conventional methods often overfitting under improperly chosen ranks or limited observations. To address these issues, we propose a Bayesian sparse tensor wheel (BTW) decomposition model within a hierarchical probabilistic framework. The main innovation of the proposed model lies in introducing a structured sparsity prior into TW decomposition, which enables automatic TW-rank determination during Bayesian inference, eliminating the need for cumbersome manual rank selection. Moreover, the Bayesian formulation naturally provides posterior uncertainty quantification for the learned latent factors, enhancing the interpretability and reliability of the decomposition results. We develop an efficient Gibbs sampling algorithm to approximate the posterior distributions. Experimental results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed BTW model, confirming its ability to autonomously determine TW-ranks and achieve superior data recovery performance compared to state-of-the-art tensor decomposition approaches.

title: Layered Janus gel with asymmetric wettability and thermo-responsive adhesion for underwater anti-oil-fouling and flexible sensing applications
Dynamic regeneration of surface-active oxygen on Pd/ZnO nanoflowers via pulsed UV light for robust room-temperature hydrogen detection
abstract: The rapid growth of the hydrogen energy industry highlights the urgent need for reliable room-temperature hydrogen leakage detection. However, the performance of most chemiresistive sensors severely deteriorates in highly humid environments due to the adsorption of water molecules. Herein, we report a robust room-temperature hydrogen sensor based on defect-engineered Pd/ZnO nanoflowers, synergistically empowered by a pulsed ultraviolet light modulation (PULM) strategy. Unlike continuous ultraviolet (UV) illumination that causes the excessive desorption of reactive oxygen species, the PULM strategy enables the dynamic regeneration of surface-active oxygen on the porous Pd/ZnO architecture. This dynamic process efficiently strips adsorbed moisture while preserving abundant active sites for interfacial hydrogen-oxygen reactions. Consequently, under a highly humid condition of 80% relative humidity, the PULM-modulated sensor exhibits a nearly eightfold enhancement in sensitivity compared to dark operation, achieving the rapid detection of 500 ppm hydrogen within 12 s. This work elucidates the mechanism of photo-modulated surface chemistry on hierarchical nanostructures, offering a highly promising pathway for practical, humidity-tolerant hydrogen safety monitoring.

title: Enhanced strengthening effect of laser shock peening through gradient thermal fields induced by localized thermal control
abstract: The strengthening effectiveness of laser shock peening (LSP) is intrinsically limited by the dynamic yield strength of high-strength alloys, which constrains both the depth and magnitude of the induced compressive residual stress (CRS). While thermal assistance can enhance plasticity, it often promotes dynamic recovery and stress relaxation, creating a thermodynamic trade-off that undermines surface integrity. To address this challenge, we propose a laser-assisted LSP (LA-LSP) strategy that employs a continuous-wave (CW) laser to generate a controllable three-dimensional gradient temperature field. By combining localized rear-surface laser heating with front-surface water confinement, a unique “thermal confinement” state is established. Numerical simulations and experiments on Ti-6Al-4V demonstrate that the gradient temperature-induced hydrostatic pressure and thermal mismatch drive intense localized shear flow, enhancing plastic deformation. Compared with conventional LSP, LA-LSP increased surface CRS by 85.3% and deepened the affected layer by 27.0%. Importantly, the gradient temperature architecture stabilizes the dislocation network, reducing thermal relaxation under high-temperature exposure from 33.6% to 22.2%. These results show that spatially controlled thermal energy can simultaneously maximize plastic strain accumulation and inhibit dynamic recovery, offering a new paradigm for strengthening hard-to-deform metallic materials.

title: Realization of load adaptivity with magnet array-based stair-step quasi-zero stiffness vibration isolators
abstract: Conventional quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) isolators are typically engineered for a specific mass or payload, and their low-frequency isolation capability deteriorates notably when the load deviates from the designated value. To address this drawback, this work proposes a magnet array-based stair-step QZS vibration isolator (MAS-QZS-VI) to achieve discrete load adaptability. The magnetic force and nonlinear magnetic stiffness of the rectangular magnet array are derived using the magnetic charge model. A parametric analysis of geometric variables is conducted to inform the design of the restoring force profile and determine the number of QZS regions. The governing equation of MAS-QZS-VI is established, and the corresponding transmissibility under different loads is derived. Numerical simulations and experimental tests are conducted to assess the load adaptability and low-frequency isolation performance of the proposed isolator. The number of QZS regions depends on the maximum magnetic negative stiffness. The designed MAS-QZS-VI can maintain considerable low-frequency vibration isolation performance when the mass is increased from 1.79 to 2.68 kg (∼49.7%). This work provides a feasible approach for realizing discrete load adaptability in stair-step QZS vibration isolator with magnet array configurations.

title: Lignin C-C bond cleavage via a photocatalytic cascade strategy
abstract: Developing sustainable biorefining technologies is a promising route for producing renewable fuels, chemicals, and materials that are independent of fossil resources. The efficient cleavage of lignin C-C bonds to produce value-added aromatics is a highly desirable goal for biorefineries, yet it remains challenging due to the robustness of recalcitrant C-C bonds. Herein, we report the efficient cleavage of lignin C-C bonds into aromatic acids via a cascade photocatalytic strategy, which overcomes the limitations of conventional non-cascade, energy-intensive approaches. Employing the lignin β-1 model as a substrate offers a near-unity yield of aromatic monomer using a polyimide photocatalyst with high photooxidation capability. Mechanistic studies reveal that C-C bond cleavage occurs via a radical-mediated photoredox process through a ketone intermediate, which significantly decreases the lignin C α -C β bond dissociation energy and facilitates its subsequent cleavage. In addition, it is found that the diaryl ketone groups in the polyimide photocatalyst are the active centers for the cascade photocatalytic process. Moreover, the cascade strategy is also applicable to converting real lignin into monomeric aromatics. This study provides an approach for efficient lignin C-C bond cleavage towards renewable aromatics with high yield, exceeding the limit set by conventional strategies.

title: Fully actuated iterative learning predictive control for spacecraft batch fly-around with batch-varying reference trajectories
abstract: This paper presents a fully actuated iterative learning predictive control (FA-ILPC) strategy for spacecraft fly-around batch missions with batch-varying reference trajectories. Unlike conventional fly-around control methods that are developed purely in the time domain with identical reference trajectories across batches, the problem is formulated in a time-batch dual domain based on the fully actuated system (FAS) approach framework. The dual domain formulation enables progressive performance improvement and enhanced tracking accuracy across batches. Motivated by the full-actuation property, a hybrid difference linear predictive model is constructed to characterize state evolution over both future time steps and batches within the predictive horizon. The proposed FA-ILPC strategy achieves structural decoupling of the multi-variable, performs dimensionality reduction, and transforms the nonlinear model into a linear predictive model, reducing system complexity, thereby simplifying controller design. To guarantee time-domain stability and batch-domain tracking error convergence, a slack optimization variable is incorporated to ensure recursive feasibility of the optimization problem. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

title: AI-driven manufacturing-limit calculation for customized tube free-bending equipment
abstract: Interference between the formed tube segment and dies is the primary cause of processing failure in tube free-bending equipment (TFBE). The boundary of the forming-parameter range within which TFBE can successfully process bent tubes is defined as the manufacturing limit. Determining this limit is particularly challenging because of the coupled effects of customized equipment structures and nonlinear tube springback behavior. This study proposes an implicit space interference inference-based manufacturing-limit calculation (ISII-MLC) framework that integrates implicit modeling and springback prediction. In the implicit-modeling stage, analytical formulations and a feature-conditioned deep signed distance function (FC-DeepSDF) are employed to construct unified implicit representations of TFBE dies. In the springback-prediction stage, an operator-fusion network (OFNet) is introduced to predict quantile sequences of bent-tube curvature and torsion. Density-calibrated conformal quantile regression (D-CQR) and a boundary-adaptive hyperrectangle (BAH) are then applied to construct joint prediction intervals. Curvature and torsion sequences sampled from these intervals are integrated using the Frenet frame to generate candidate springback axes, which are embedded into the implicit space of TFBE for interference inference and manufacturing-limit determination. A case study is conducted to validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that FC-DeepSDF enables accurate implicit modeling and reliable structural modification, while the combination of OFNet, D-CQR, and BAH yields robust and compact joint prediction intervals. The obtained manufacturing limits are consistent with experimental observations, indicating that the proposed framework provides an effective method for assessing the manufacturing capability of customized TFBE.

title: A gearbox condition difference monitoring mechanism under one-class data
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) methods have achieved significant success in gearbox condition monitoring. However, it is difficult to obtain fault data for different operating conditions of new equipment in practical engineering applications, which is one of the main limitations of AI methods for condition monitoring. This research suggests a condition difference monitoring mechanism (CDMM) based on one-class data to overcome this problem. Based on a dataset of transmission operating under healthy conditions, the characteristics of the data in a healthy state are summarized. A harmonic modulation bispectrum structure is established to enhance data dimensionality, thereby achieving deep dissection of hidden features in the data. Design differentiated diagnostic models using support vector data description to improve the interpretability of training and discrimination processes. It is possible to lessen the impact of noise on the target and improve fault detection accuracy by building differentiated weights based on the discreteness between the target domain and the features of the health model. Experimental results obtained from planetary and parallel gearbox test rigs demonstrate the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed CDMM, highlighting its practical value for condition monitoring of industrial gear transmission systems under limited fault data availability.

title: Event-based prescribed time inverse optimal control for multi-agent systems
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of distributed prescribed time inverse optimal consensus control for nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) by using dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM). First, a time-varying constraint function is constructed to transform the prescribed time consensus problem into a control problem characterized by deferred constraints with respect to synchronization errors. This constraint function has no restrictions on the initial state, while settling time and tracking accuracy can be manually set in advance. Then, based on the inverse optimal practical stabilization criterion, a distributed neural prescribed time inverse optimal control strategy is devised to circumvent the need for solving the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, thereby reducing the computational effort. To decrease the frequency of controller updates, a DETM is established that enables the design of appropriate dynamic event rules without modifying the framework of the inverse optimal controller. As a result, the event-based prescribed time inverse optimal control strategy guarantees that all signals in the closed-loop system are bounded. Finally, simulation results verify the feasibility of the established control methodology.

title: A wearable multifunctional liquid-metal sensory interface with multimodal and multi-target sensing capabilities for smart home applications
abstract: High-performance sensors have garnered attention for smart home development. However, many proposed sensors are hindered from achieving widespread applications due to their complex units, feeding designs, high cost, single-mode sensing capabilities, and insufficient sensitivity. Here, we introduce a wearable multifunctional liquid-metal sensory interface (WMLSI) built on a liquid metal spoof localized surface plasmon (SLSP) sensor array. The WMLSI enables simultaneous multi-target sensing, along with multimodal sensing. Distinct physical interaction mechanisms are employed: strain- and temperature-sensing rely on contact-induced physical deformation of the sensing units, whereas biosensing leverages evanescent waves with non-contact dielectric interactions. Additionally, biosensing is dedicated to in vitro diagnostics and is thus functionally isolated from the strain- and temperature-sensing modules designed for wearable applications. Strain- and temperature-sensing are decoupled owing to distinct fabrication processes. Each individual SLSP sensing unit is designed with independent resonances to prevent inter-unit coupling. All sensing units are coupled via a single microstrip line for feeding, which significantly reduces manufacturing complexity and power consumption while concurrently mitigating the risk of feed structure fracture caused by metal fatigue during motion. The proposed WMLSI significantly broadens the application scope for next-generation electronic skin and smart home technologies.

title: An intelligent perception–decision system for enhancing performance of underwater gliders under unknown three-dimensional shear flow fields
abstract: Operating in unknown three-dimensional (3D) shear-flow fields can significantly degrade the motion performance of underwater gliders (UGs). As resource-constrained platforms, UGs possess limited sensing capabilities and cannot directly determine the complete flow field. Moreover, traditional empirical control strategies struggle to maintain long-term performance stability. To address these challenges, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven intelligent perception–decision system (IPDS) that integrates physics-based modeling with data-driven inference has been developed to support environmental perception and decision-making under partially observable conditions.
