The perception module identifies 3D flow information from limited motion data. A surrogate model is designed based on a physics-informed multi-branch neural network (MBNN) to extract high-confidence flow features from Ugs’ dynamic responses, and a two-stage parameter assimilation mechanism is developed to reconstruct the 3D flow structure. Using the identified flow information, the decision module optimizes the navigation strategy to maximize the motion performance. A rapid performance evaluation model based on a radial basis function neural network (RBFNN) is integrated with the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to dynamically optimize the control parameters, balancing energy efficiency and trajectory accuracy. IPDS, the depth-averaged current (DAC) model, and empirical fixed-control strategies were compared using simulation analysis. The simulation results show that IPDS improves the trajectory accuracy by 93.88% compared with empirical strategies and by 57.55% compared with DAC strategies. Sea trials using Petrel-UL UGs further validated the effectiveness of the system. This study highlights the potential of AI-driven perception and decision frameworks for enhancing the autonomy of resource-constrained robotic systems operating in uncertain real-world environments.

title: Breathable sensing papers for human health multi-signal monitoring
abstract: Wearable sensors capable of detecting multiple forms of signals hold great promise for human health monitoring. However, current research has largely focused on improving sensing performance, with less attention devoted to the comfort of wearable devices. As a result, reports on comfortable yet versatile sensors remain scarce. In this work, we present a multifunctional wearable sensing paper based on highly breathable lens paper. This capacitive-type sensing paper enables multimodal signal perception, including pressure, proximity, humidity, and metabolites in sweat. The sensor exhibits high pressure sensitivity (∼0.63 kPa −1 ), fast response/recovery time (150 ms/80 ms), and a SERS detection limit as low as 10 −9 mol L −1 for R6G, along with excellent breathability for comfortable long-term wear. Porous lens paper has been employed as both a dielectric layer and breathable electrode substrate (after Au deposition), as well as a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) substrate. The sensing paper is lightweight and flexible, demonstrating high sensitivity, fast response, and stability in pressure detection. Its high breathability ensures wearing comfort and also enables capacitive humidity sensing. Furthermore, the natural plasmonic structure of the gold-coated lens paper makes it an efficient SERS substrate for detecting sweat metabolites. These versatile sensing papers can be comfortably attached to human skin and facilitate long-term monitoring of multiple physiological signals, showing considerable potential for cutting-edge applications in human health monitoring.

title: Multiscale mapping of structure-activity relationships in Y-Sr-Mn oxides toward efficient solar thermochemical CO2 conversion
abstract: Abstract Solar-driven thermochemical CO 2 splitting is a promising pathway for carbon-neutral fuel production. However, its practical deployment is hindered by the limited redox capacity and insufficient high-temperature stability of conventional oxide materials. Perovskite-type oxides (ABO 3 ) have emerged as strong candidates due to their tunable oxygen non-stoichiometry and structural robustness under extreme conditions. In this work, we systematically investigate the influence of A-site cation engineering through yttrium and strontium substitution in Y x Sr 1− x MnO 3 ( x = 0.1–0.6) perovskites using both micro-scale and system-scale approaches. Among the compositions, Y 0.40 Sr 0.60 MnO 3 (Y4SM) demonstrated the most favorable thermochemical performance, supported by density functional theory and kinetic analyses that reveal enhanced redox activity and oxygen exchanges. Porous Y4SM composites were further fabricated and tested in a solar-simulator-driven reactor, bridging intrinsic material properties with practical CO 2 splitting performance. The material exhibited a record-high CO yield of 37.39 mmol/g per cycle and a peak production rate of 9.96 mL/(min g) at relatively low operating temperatures (950/890 °C). Multi-cycle tests confirm excellent stability, with an average peak rate of 69.97 mL/min. These results highlight the effectiveness of A-site engineering in perovskites and demonstrate the strong potential of Y4SM for efficient, scalable solar thermochemical CO 2 conversion.

title: An advanced k-ε based non-uniform eigenvalue perturbation method for uncertainty quantification in full-stage centrifugal compressor
abstract: Abstract Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) models remain the dominant tool for turbomachinery design and analysis, yet their predictive accuracy is constrained by structural uncertainties inherent in the eddy-viscosity assumption. To quantify the uncertainty of the RANS turbulence model, this study employs a non-parametric approach that perturbs the eigenvalues of the Reynolds stress tensor and successfully applies it to the analysis of a full-stage centrifugal compressor. The non-uniform perturbation method adopted in this study effectively resolves the convergence difficulties that conventional uniform-perturbation approaches encounter in complex simulation cases. Unlike prior perturbation frameworks designed mainly for the SST k - ω model, this study introduces such perturbation methods for the first time on the k - ε turbulence model. To maintain consistency with the wall-function treatment, a near-wall perturbation damping function is incorporated. Flow-field analysis indicates that the perturbations modify turbulence anisotropy, thereby influencing separation behaviour and component characteristics. In addition, the perturbation-induced variations in flow angles modify rotor-stator matching, thereby affecting the overall performance. The confidence intervals generated under the imposed perturbations successfully envelop all the experimental data, demonstrating that the proposed framework can effectively quantify the inherent structural uncertainty in RANS-based predictions and account for the discrepancies between the numerical simulations and the experimental measurements.

title: Regrowth behavior and tribological properties of sputtered molybdenum disulfide films in different polar media
Finite-time adaptive output consensus of uncertain higher-order multi-agent systems under matched/mismatched disturbances
abstract: This paper investigates the finite-time output consensus problem for high-order uncertain leader-follower multi-agent systems (MASs) under matched/mismatched disturbances. To address the complex challenges arising from the coexistence of unknown parameters, matched disturbances, and mismatched disturbances in the considered leader-follower MASs, a novel distributed adaptive control protocol is developed. First, a finite-time disturbance observer is designed to reconstruct the disturbances and their required derivatives within a finite time, thereby compensating for the effects of matched/mismatched disturbances. Second, an integral-type non-singular terminal sliding-mode surface is constructed using neighboring state information and disturbance estimates to establish finite-time stability of the higher-order consensus errors. Finally, an adaptive law incorporating a projection operator and a σ -modification term is designed to compensate for the unknown system parameters online. The proposed distributed controller guarantees finite-time output consensus of the closed-loop system without requiring inversion of the augmented Laplacian matrix. Rigorous theoretical analysis establishes the boundedness of the closed-loop signals before observer convergence and finite-time output consensus thereafter. Two simulation examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
